newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil mulls leasing, rediscount changes - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil mulls leasing, rediscount changes - paper.

text.p: Brazil's National Monetary Council will meet this afternoon to consider removing restrictions on consumer leasing and expanding the use of rediscount credit lines to banks, Gazeta Mercantil said.
The paper said the council, made up of the nation's top economic policymakers, was considering freeing up consumer leasing and setting a minimum period of 90 days for any operation.
Gazeta also said the council would consider increasing access to its rediscount credit lines, which amounted to 4.6 billion reais in July.

Officials were mulling the idea of determining the volume of rediscount credit by basing it not only on an average of cash deposits, as it is now, but also on an average of timed deposits, Gazeta said.

The paper said the council would also look at whether it wanted to maintain the Central Bank's Basic Interest Rate (TBC) for rediscount transactions or if it wanted to create another rate to reflect the changes in determining the volume of rediscount credit available.
Gazeta said a plan to discuss a credit line for Minas Gerais state bank Credireal was dropped because it was not compatible with a recently announced federal program to help ailing state banks.
